segments.say: Over a hundred and thirty thousand Outlook outage reports. At the peak.
segments.show: Microsoft 365 went down on Thursday 12 Nov. Downdetector reports for Outlook peaked at over 130,000 around 1:15 p.m. ET, per Newsweek. Microsoft said users in any region could be affected.

segments.say: Myth: it must be a hack. Reality: Microsoft has disclosed no evidence of a cyberattack.
segments.show: Per SecurityWeek, a large number of servers became unavailable and were failing automated health checks. Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and Defender XDR were affected. Incidents EX1550543 / MO1550821.
segments.card: No evidence of an attack disclosed

segments.say: Recovery was still partial after five hours. Keep a backup channel, and warn staff about fake fix your mailbox emails.
segments.show: Reuters, via The Korea Times, reported limited recovery after more than five hours. Sources: Newsweek, SecurityWeek, The Korea Times (12–13 Nov).
segments.card: Backup comms · watch for outage phishing

items.ig_caption:
Over 130,000 Outlook outage reports at the peak. And no, Microsoft hasn't said it was a hack. 📉

What was reported (12–13 Nov):
→ Microsoft 365 went down on Thursday 12 Nov; reports began around 12:30 p.m. ET and Outlook peaked at over 130,000 Downdetector reports around 1:15 p.m. ET (Newsweek)
→ Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Defender XDR were affected, and Microsoft said users in any region could be hit (SecurityWeek, Newsweek)
→ Microsoft said a large number of servers became unavailable and were failing automated health checks; it has yet to explain why (SecurityWeek)
→ Microsoft has disclosed no evidence of a cyberattack (SecurityWeek)
→ After more than five hours, Microsoft reported only limited recovery (Reuters, via The Korea Times)

What to do: track incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, keep a non-Microsoft channel for incident comms, and warn staff that outages bring fake "re-verify your mailbox" emails.
